leagues.name: Torneo Federal A
leagues.note: AR3R (the Reválida path, 19 clubs) was merged into this row: the competition is one 37-club tournament with two paths, not two leagues.

boundaries.selection: down: (a) last place of the three-season promedio table (2024+2025+2026 regular phases, points / matches played, newly promoted clubs counting only from their promotion season) and (b) last place of the season's aggregate table (Apertura + Clausura regular phases). If the same club is last in both, it goes down by promedio and (b) passes to the penultimate place (29th) of the aggregate; ties in a relegation place are play-off matches. up: Primera Nacional final winner (zone winners, one-off final) + Torneo Reducido winner
boundaries.note: Exactly two down and two up every season, any club regardless of affiliation or geography. 2026: Estudiantes (RC) was last in both tables and went down by promedio (0.437), so the aggregate slot passed to Aldosivi (29th of 30, 19 pts); Godoy Cruz went up as Primera Nacional champion. The general rule is last of the aggregate table, not always the penultimate: the 29th is the overlap case. The English page compresses (b) to 'last in the aggregate table'.

boundaries.selection: down: bottom two of each of the two Primera Nacional zones (4 clubs), each sent to the level-3 branch of its AFA affiliation - Primera B Metropolitana if directly affiliated / Buenos Aires metropolitan area, Torneo Federal A if indirectly affiliated (regional leagues) / outside Greater Buenos Aires. up: Torneo Federal A champion + Torneo Federal A Revalida winner + Primera B Metropolitana champion + Primera B Metropolitana Reducido winner = 2 from each branch
boundaries.note: Totals are fixed (4 down, 4 up) but the per-branch split is not: 2026 sent 3 down to Primera B Metropolitana (Acassuso, San Miguel, Nueva Chicago) and 1 to Torneo Federal A (Guemes, Santiago del Estero). 2025 sent 3 to Primera B (Arsenal, Talleres (RdE), Defensores Unidos) and 1 to Federal A (Alvarado). Do not hardcode 2/2.

boundaries.selection: down: Torneo Federal A bottom two of each Revalida zone on the combined table (4, to the interior branch's 4th tier) + Primera B Metropolitana bottom two of the single table (2, to Primera C). up: from Primera C to Primera B Metropolitana (2 in the 2025 edition; 2026 count not published) and from the 4th-tier interior tournament to Federal A
boundaries.note: Included because level 3 cannot be resized without it. The interior 4th tier changes in 2027: the Torneo Regional Federal Amateur is replaced by the Torneo Argentino del Interior, which takes the 4 Federal A 2026 relegations and grants 6 promotions to Federal A (not the 4 TRFA used in 2026). Up-counts from level 4 are therefore left null.

conflicts: ARGC is a phase, not a competition: the 2026 top division is Apertura + Clausura + aggregate table. The Apertura row (same 30 clubs) is missing, so the 'Campeon de Liga' title and one of the two relegation slots cannot be computed from the database.
Level-1 relegation is not resolvable from the ARGC row at all: it needs the season aggregate table (both tournaments) and a 2024-2026 promedio table, and 2024/2025 data is absent.

AR3F (18) and AR3R (19) are two paths of one 37-club competition (Torneo Federal A 2026), not two competitions. 18+19=37 is only the entry split after the first phase; clubs eliminated from the championship path are re-fed into the Revalida, so one club can appear in both rows within a season and the Revalida's final field exceeds 19.

Level 3 is two parallel branches, not one league: Torneo Federal A (37 clubs, indirectly affiliated) and Primera B Metropolitana (22 clubs, directly affiliated). The three level-3 rows sum to 59, which is the correct total, but treating those 59 as one league is wrong - clubs only cross branches through Primera Nacional relegation, by affiliation.
The level-3 downward edge is missing entirely (Federal A: 4 down; Primera B: 2 down). Without those rows, clubs relegated from level 3 have nowhere to go and level-3 sizes cannot be maintained.

Missing rows: Torneo Apertura 2026 (level 1, 30 clubs), Primera C Metropolitana (level 4, directly affiliated), Torneo Argentino del Interior 2027 / Torneo Regional Federal Amateur (level 4, indirectly affiliated).

Source conflict: the English Torneo Federal A page says 20 clubs entered the Revalida first phase; the Spanish page and arithmetic (37 - 18) give 19, which matches our row. The English page also says Federal A relegation goes to the Torneo Regional Federal Amateur, while the Spanish page (newer) says the Torneo Argentino del Interior, which replaces the TRFA as 4th tier from 2027.
Primera Nacional totals are stable but the branch split is not: 2026 relegated 3 to Primera B Metropolitana and 1 to Torneo Federal A. Any model that assigns a fixed 2/2 will break the branch sizes.
